\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کلاهبردار} (kolâhbardâr)}{کلاهبردار (kolâhbardâr)}]{\fa{کلاهبردار} (kolâhbardâr) — a con man, a swindler}

\label{lesson:FA-C323-kolahbardar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for bail, then the Persian for to be released.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کلاهبردار}}
\textbf{\fa{کلاهبردار}} (\emph{kolâhbardâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}a con man, a swindler\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{یک} \fa{کلاهبردار} \fa{پول} \fa{پیرزن} \fa{را} \fa{گرفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Yek kolâhbardâr pul-e pirzan râ gereft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A con man took the old woman's money.
\end{quote}

Literally \textquotedblleft{}hat-lifter\textquotedblright{}: \emph{kolâh} \textquotedblleft{}hat\textquotedblright{} + \emph{bardâr} \textquotedblleft{}one who lifts\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Kolâh-e kasi râ bardâshtan} \textquotedblleft{}to cheat someone\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kolâhbardâr} is built from Persian \emph{kolâh} \textquotedblleft{}hat\textquotedblright{} and \emph{bardâr-}, the stem of \emph{bardâshtan} \textquotedblleft{}to lift, to take away\textquotedblright{}: the one who takes your hat. All of it is native.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kolâhbardâr}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kolâhbardâr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{kolâhbardâr}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for bail, then the Persian for to be released, then say \emph{kolâhbardâr} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{کلاهبردار} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A con man, a swindler\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{فریب} \fa{دادن} (farib dâdan)}{فریب دادن (farib dâdan)}]{\fa{فریب} \fa{دادن} (farib dâdan) — to deceive, to trick}

\label{lesson:FA-C323-farib-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to be released, then the Persian for a con man.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{فریب} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{فریب} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{farib dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to deceive, to trick\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{با} \fa{یک} \fa{نامه} \fa{جعلی} \fa{مردم} \fa{را} \fa{فریب} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U bâ yek nâme-ye ja'li mardom râ farib dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He tricked people with a fake letter.
\end{quote}

\emph{Farib khordan} is \textquotedblleft{}to be fooled\textquotedblright{}. Present \emph{farib midahad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{farib} \textquotedblleft{}deceit\textquotedblright{} is a native Persian word; EtymDB lists it without a parent. \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{farib dâdan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{farib dâdan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{farib dâdan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to be released, then the Persian for a con man, then say \emph{farib dâdan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{فریب} \fa{دادن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To deceive, to trick\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تهدید} \fa{کردن} (tahdid kardan)}{تهدید کردن (tahdid kardan)}]{\fa{تهدید} \fa{کردن} (tahdid kardan) — to threaten}

\label{lesson:FA-C323-tahdid-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a con man, then the Persian for to deceive.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تهدید} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تهدید} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{tahdid kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to threaten\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مرد} \fa{فروشنده} \fa{را} \fa{تهدید} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mard forushande râ tahdid kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The man threatened the shopkeeper.
\end{quote}

The threat takes \emph{be}. Present \emph{tahdid mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tahdid} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{tahdīd}, \textquotedblleft{}a threat\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists both the Arabic and the Persian word). \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tahdid kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tahdid kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tahdid kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a con man, then the Persian for to deceive, then say \emph{tahdid kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{تهدید} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To threaten\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دعوا} \fa{کردن} (da'vâ kardan)}{دعوا کردن (da'vâ kardan)}]{\fa{دعوا} \fa{کردن} (da'vâ kardan) — to quarrel, to have a fight}

\label{lesson:FA-C323-dava-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to deceive, then the Persian for to threaten.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دعوا} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{دعوا} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{da'vâ kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to quarrel, to have a fight\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دو} \fa{راننده} \fa{در} \fa{خیابان} \fa{دعوا} \fa{کردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Do rânande dar khiyâbân da'vâ kardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Two drivers had a fight in the street.
\end{quote}

The other side takes \emph{bâ}: \emph{bâ hamsâye da'vâ kard}. Present \emph{da'vâ mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{da'vâ} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{da'wā}, \textquotedblleft{}a claim, an assertion\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); in Persian it became an everyday word for a quarrel. \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{da'vâ kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{da'vâ kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{da'vâ kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to deceive, then the Persian for to threaten, then say \emph{da'vâ kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کتک} \fa{زدن} (kotak zadan)}{کتک زدن (kotak zadan)}]{\fa{کتک} \fa{زدن} (kotak zadan) — to beat (up), to hit}

\label{lesson:FA-C323-kotak-zadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to threaten, then the Persian for to quarrel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کتک} \fa{زدن}}
\textbf{\fa{کتک} \fa{زدن}} (\emph{kotak zadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to beat (up), to hit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دزدها} \fa{نگهبان} \fa{را} \fa{کتک} \fa{زدند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dozd-hâ negahbân râ kotak zadand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The thieves beat up the guard.
\end{quote}

\emph{Kotak khordan} is \textquotedblleft{}to get a beating\textquotedblright{}. Present \emph{kotak mizanad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kotak} \textquotedblleft{}blows\textquotedblright{} is a native word whose origin is not settled; \emph{zadan} \textquotedblleft{}to strike\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian. EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 316–323 — a review}

\label{lesson:FA-R323-review-316-323}



\begin{quote}
Say the Persian for a thief and a theft.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a thief, a theft, a robber, a pickpocket, a bag snatcher
  \item to chase, to hide, to flee, to disappear, to be found out
  \item a serious crime, a murder, a murderer, to attack, a weapon
  \item an officer, a patrol, a suspect, to be arrested, to detain
  \item a detective, a clue, a footprint, a fingerprint, an interrogation
  \item to swear, to testify, to admit, to give away, guilty
  \item to be sentenced, to be acquitted, a prisoner, bail, to be released
  \item a con man, to deceive, to threaten, to quarrel, to beat
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A thief? (\textbf{\fa{دزد}}.) A theft? (\textbf{\fa{دزدی}}.) A robber? (\textbf{\fa{سارق}}.) A pickpocket? (\textbf{\fa{جیب} \fa{بر}}.) A bag snatcher? (\textbf{\fa{کیف} \fa{قاپ}}.) To chase? (\textbf{\fa{تعقیب} \fa{کردن}}.) To hide? (\textbf{\fa{قایم} \fa{شدن}}.) To flee? (\textbf{\fa{گریختن}}.) To disappear? (\textbf{\fa{ناپدید} \fa{شدن}}.) To be found out? (\textbf{\fa{لو} \fa{رفتن}}.) A serious crime? (\textbf{\fa{جنایت}}.) A murder? (\textbf{\fa{قتل}}.) A murderer? (\textbf{\fa{قاتل}}.) To attack? (\textbf{\fa{حمله} \fa{کردن}}.) A weapon? (\textbf{\fa{اسلحه}}.) An officer? (\textbf{\fa{مامور}}.) A patrol? (\textbf{\fa{گشت}}.) A suspect? (\textbf{\fa{مظنون}}.) To be arrested? (\textbf{\fa{دستگیر} \fa{شدن}}.) To detain? (\textbf{\fa{بازداشت} \fa{کردن}}.) A detective? (\textbf{\fa{کارآگاه}}.) A clue? (\textbf{\fa{سرنخ}}.) A footprint? (\textbf{\fa{ردپا}}.) A fingerprint? (\textbf{\fa{اثر} \fa{انگشت}}.) An interrogation? (\textbf{\fa{بازجویی}}.) To swear? (\textbf{\fa{قسم} \fa{خوردن}}.) To testify? (\textbf{\fa{شهادت} \fa{دادن}}.) To admit? (\textbf{\fa{اقرار} \fa{کردن}}.) To give away? (\textbf{\fa{لو} \fa{دادن}}.) Guilty? (\textbf{\fa{گناهکار}}.) To be sentenced? (\textbf{\fa{محکوم} \fa{شدن}}.) To be acquitted? (\textbf{\fa{تبرئه} \fa{شدن}}.) A prisoner? (\textbf{\fa{زندانی}}.) Bail? (\textbf{\fa{وثیقه}}.) To be released? (\textbf{\fa{آزاد} \fa{شدن}}.) A con man? (\textbf{\fa{کلاهبردار}}.) To deceive? (\textbf{\fa{فریب} \fa{دادن}}.) To threaten? (\textbf{\fa{تهدید} \fa{کردن}}.) To quarrel? (\textbf{\fa{دعوا} \fa{کردن}}.) To beat? (\textbf{\fa{کتک} \fa{زدن}}.)
